title: Grid layout
description:
A dashboard laid out with **CSS Grid** terms: column and row tracks, named areas and
panels placed by name or by row and column. Resize the window to see the `fr` column
and the `1fr` row follow it. See `:help dbdash-layout`.

query.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE h(n) AS (SELECT 0 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM h WHERE n < 23)
SELECT printf('%02d', n) AS hour, 50 + abs(random() % 100) AS visits FROM h

show.title: trend: area across two columns, row auto
show.description:
`show.area: trend` puts this panel in the **trend** area (CSS `grid-area`), which
spans the first two columns. Its row is `auto`: at least the plot's
`min_height` (6 rows here, 8 by default), growing up to its full height (15) when
the window has room.

show.title: kpi: two rows
show.description:
The **kpi** area is two rows tall (CSS `grid-row: span 2`) in the fixed
24-column track (`columns: "2fr 1fr 24"`).

query.sql:
SELECT 'North' AS region, 120 AS sales UNION ALL SELECT 'South', 80
UNION ALL SELECT 'East', 95 UNION ALL SELECT 'West', 60

show.title: table: a fixed row of 9 lines
show.description:
The second row is `9` lines (a fixed track, like `grid-template-rows: ... 9 ...`):
a fixed row keeps its size whatever the window.

query.sql:
SELECT 'IT' AS dept, 42 AS people UNION ALL SELECT 'HR', 7
UNION ALL SELECT 'R&D', 120

show.title: share
show.description: The **share** area: the `1fr` column of the second row.

query.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE d(n) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM d WHERE n < 30)
SELECT n AS day, abs(random() % 100) AS load FROM d

show.title: wide: minmax(10, 1fr) fills the rest of the window
show.description:
The third row is `minmax(10, 1fr)`: at least 10 lines, and whatever the window has
left (CSS `fr`). A chart in a fixed or `fr` row fills its cell, so this one grows
with the window.

show.title: rows 4-5, columns 2-3: placed by position
show.description:
`row: 4`, `column: 2`, `span: 2`, `row_span: 2` (CSS
`grid-row: 4 / span 2; grid-column: 2 / span 2`). Rows 4 and 5 are past
`layout.rows`, so they use `auto_rows`.

query.sql: SELECT 'flows into the first free cell' AS note

show.title: auto-placed
show.description:
No area, row or column: the panel flows into the first free cell (CSS
auto-placement), here row 4, column 1.
